newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker, shrugs of strike, stocks.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker, shrugs of strike, stocks.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker despite a larger-than-expected drop in LME stocks Friday and news of a strike at a Chilean mine.
December copper ended 1.20 cents off at 94.35 cents a lb.

LME stocks fell 7,775 tonnes to 113,400 tonnes. Stocks in Singapore rose a nominal 200 tonnes - some traders have been expecting a sizeable increase. A 2,800-tonne drawdown in Long Beach stocks in California was also seen as bullish by some.

During the same period covered by the LME report, COMEX stocks were fairly flat, a sign that the arbitrage related deliveries from LME to COMEX depots have largely ended for the time being, and that metal from Long Beach was for consumption in the U.S. or shipment to the Far East, traders said.
The market shrugged off news of a strike since Monday at Phelps Dodge Corp's Candelaria mine in Chile. The company said production was unaffected as the pit was being worked by non-unionized labor.

"While output has not been lost, if it continues, it could be lost," said minerals economist Fred Demler of E D and F Man International. "We had a major move on the upside this week, and we saw a little bit of profit-taking and some booksquaring."
Volume was moderate at an estimated 15,000 lots, up from Thursday's official 13,800 lots.
December ended up 1.70 cents on the week.
Earlier some brokers noted talk that influential shorts in the market could still be forced to cover, pushing up prices between now and December.

"There is also talk that some of the large speculators have covered back some of their short positions, and that they have bought some calls for the nearby, for December to help cover their short position," an industry source said.
Meanwhile, Phelps Dodge and labor unions at the company's Chino mine in New Mexico were scheduled to meet Friday in a bid to end the stalemate in drawing up a new contract.
The previous Chino contract expired on June 30.
COMEX stocks Friday rose 402 short tons to 31,431 tons.
